isolation_policy.credential_handling: The six named database/runtime/acceptance environment variables were explicitly unset for every Python command. Their values were not inspected, printed, or persisted. The actual CLI subprocess inherited the same sanitized environment.
isolation_policy.temporary_bundle_handling: Each fixture was serialized by the existing production serializer into a distinct OS temporary directory represented here as <temporary-bundle-root>; the directory was automatically removed after its real CLI invocation. No checked-in fixture was changed.

included: Gate B S_direct-to-S_okf span identity for all three frozen fixture classes
Actual scripts/rebuild_from_okf.py --verify-roundtrip subprocess parity using temporary serializer-produced bundles
non_goals: Live Docling conversion or frozen-fixture regeneration
Modification of source, tests, fixtures, README, planning, package, or git state
Stage, commit, push, or Phase 15 authorization

caveats: Normal frozen-fixture validation is offline and verifies the frozen direct-chain outputs; it does not rerun live Docling conversion.
Only sanitized counts, stream lengths, and SHA-256 digests are retained; raw terminal output, temporary paths, fixture text, and environment values are not retained.
A third-party import warning was observed in the parent Python process during commands and is intentionally not retained; every captured real CLI subprocess stream was empty.
